results.title: Summer 2026 Anime Rankings – Week 5
results.snippet:
The fifth weekly poll for the Summer 2026 anime season has concluded, and *Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia* has returned to the top of the rankings.
After finishing fifth last week, the series climbed four spots to take first place with 6.75% of the vote.
*Though I Am an Inept Villainess* followed closely behind with 6.32%, holding onto a top-three spot for the fourth consecutive week.
Last week’s winner, *Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity*, dropped to third with 6.26%, just 0.06 percentage points behind second place.
*Saga of Tanya the Evil II* remained in fourth, while *Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation Season 3* rounded out the top five.
As always, these rankings reflect the preferences of the Anime Corner community and are not intended to determine what anyone should or should not watch.

results.title: Mii-chan and Miss Yamada Staff Issue Statement After Backlash to Anime News
results.snippet:
Critics assert anime will alienate those with intellectual, developmental disabilities
The production committee for the Mii-chan and Miss Yamada anime issued a statement last week regarding criticism over the anime's announcement and how it might affect people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
...
The committee stated last week that it acknowledges the concerns and opinions regarding the upcoming anime, and added, “While respecting the themes and messages of the original *[manga]*, we will carefully proceed with the production and consult with experts to ensure we do not foster prejudice or misunderstanding, including appropriate ratings and disclaimers.”
The statement came just over a day after the anime's announcement on July 26.
The production committee's statement has itself drawn some criticism.
Users on social media suggested that the anime's staff ask people to stop using “Mii-chan” as a nickname to disparage people, generally girls and women, with intellectual or developmental disabilities.

results.title: After Just 1 Episode, The Ghost in the Shell Is Officially 2026's Most Overhated Anime
results.snippet:
Just a day after The Ghost in the Shell 's premiere on July 7, the internet was already swarming with utterly bad takes about Science SARU's new addition to the most iconic cyberpunk anime franchise of all time.
...
Perhaps the best embodiment of the controversy right now comes from a viral comparison being made between one shared scene from Mamoru Oshii's Ghost in the Shell film in 1995 and the 2026 Science SARU adapation.
...
Many anime fans familiar with the original film (and still others who never even saw either the OG or the new series) have vocally begun decrying the new adaptation for 'watering down' the original vision, or even censoring something great to turn the series into a shell of its former self.
While it's hard to match the imagery of Kusanagi diving nude from a building, what most are failing to realize is that Science SARU's version of the iconic building diving scene is completely true to the vision of the source material that started it all: Masamune Shirow's 1989 manga The Ghost in the Shell .
And anyone still concerned that Ghost in the Shell is completely censoring its sexuality need only wait until Episode 2 of the new series drops.
